text:
anya: Heads up — pushed a sandbox prototype for a "Fallback Heuristic Editor". Want quick UX feedback before I wire telemetry. Playground: https://sandbox.redwood.internal/heuristics (private).

mike: nice. what's the intended scope? classifying errors, choosing degrade modes, or both?

anya: both. idea is one place operators can: 1) define triggers (latency/error patterns), 2) classify the trigger (transient, persistent, noisy), 3) pick a degrade action (soft-sample/quiet-fallback/full-cutover), and 4) attach audit tags + retention.

jordan: can it surface example request traces inline? makes it easier to judge false positives.

anya: yes — preview pane shows sampled traces + token-level latency histograms. also a small simulator to apply rule against historical trace slices.

sam: audit concern: need immutable record of who changed a rule and why. we should link to a CI-style changelist (PR) or at least a signed audit entry.

mike: agreed. also want a clear default ordering for degrade modes. e.g., try soft-sample -> cache-prefix -> fallback model -> full degrade. operators shouldn't accidentally jump straight to full degrade.

anya: default ordering is configurable per-policy, but we show a recommended flow with a compact UI affordance. open to wording.

jordan: accessibility nit: the ordering control needs keyboard-friendly drag handles or a numbered list + up/down buttons.

anya: good call. will add up/down and confirm modal to prevent accidental full-degrade.

mike: how are triggers expressed? regex on error message? percentiles? combination?

anya: flexible DSL + structured options. quick examples in editor:

```
# example rule
trigger: latency_p95>700ms for 5m OR http_5xx_rate>3% for 1m
classification: transient
actions:
  - soft_sample(rate=0.1, duration=10m)
  - route_to: fallback-v2
audIT_note: "auto-sim run on canary; flagged by build-189"
```

sam: great to have explicit durations. also, ensure we log the exact matching signal id and the trace ids used for simulation. auditability hinges on reproducible evidence.

jordan: UI idea: when picking classification, show suggested downstream consequences — e.g., transient -> keep caching, increase sampling; persistent -> escalate to operator notify + gradual cutover.

anya: that's the intent. we show a compact explanation inline and an example diff of what will change in routing.

mike: about telemetry: do we emit a rule_evaluation event every time a rule fires? that could be high-traffic.

anya: we plan sampled eval events + counters. full evaluation tracer only on sampled matches. rate-limitable.

sam: also add a tamper-evidence hash on saved rules so post-hoc audits can verify integrity. minimal overhead but useful for compliance.

anya: nice, I'll add.

deploy-bot: build 2026.03.21-heuristic-editor deployed to sandbox :white_check_mark:

mike: one more UX ask — surface a "why did this fire" affordance with the top 3 signals that contributed (and weight). makes debugging much faster.

anya: yep — importance weights + link to the raw metric plumbing.

jordan: can we preview the fallback model latency/cost impact inline? ops always asks about cost.

anya: simulator includes token-cost delta and p50/p95 latency estimates for the selected fallback target.

sam: next steps: (1) add immutable changelog + tamper hash, (2) keyboard accessible ordering control, (3) explainability panel with top signals, (4) sampled eval telemetry + counters. can we get a quick UX review tomorrow?

anya: yes — I'll update the sandbox and post a short checklist. thanks all :thumbsup:

mike: +1, I'll bring this to oncall huddle if there are any safety concerns.

jordan: love the simulator — big win for operator confidence.

anya: filing followups: #1 changelog/integrity, #2 accessibility, #3 telemetry sampling knobs. ping me if you want edit access to the sandbox.

sam: please add a short runbook snippet that maps classification -> operator escalation policy. helps triage.

anya: will do. planning a quick demo 11:00 tomorrow.

mike: see you there.
